inspiration: Drake burner as a data record: one unit file holds a list of attacks (claws as melee, fire breath as a type of attack), each with its own icon, damage and strike count (data/core/units/drakes/Burner.cfg lines 27-40). Recreate the attack-record shape, not the drake.

Strike animation as a frame range with a per-frame time: a melee strip of six frames written as one range at 100 ms per frame (Burner.cfg line 59). Our hero and creature clip syntax can copy the idea with our own timing curves.

Team colour as four values per faction: average, highlight, shadow and minimap marker (data/core/team-colors.cfg line 4 and the rest of the file). Palette-swap team colour from one ramp; reusable for faction colour.

Attack preview as an exact per-round table: the combat code builds the HP-by-HP probability matrix for both sides, handles slowed states as separate planes, and switches to a sampled estimate above a complexity threshold (src/attack_prediction.cpp 1853-1870, 2366-2380; header constant 50000). Shape only: GPL, clean-room.
Monte Carlo fallback with a fixed sample count: 5000 iterations per run (src/attack_prediction.cpp 1408-1500). A cheap estimate for big fights, exact odds for small ones.

Debuff math with clamping: calculate_probability_of_debuff clamps touch and kill probabilities to 0-1 and notes float drift (src/attack_prediction.cpp 1755-1770). Useful for our poison and slow stacks.
Per-unit death sound as a named file on the unit record (die_sound=drake-die.ogg, Burner.cfg line 19). Simple, data-driven death cue per creature.

briefs.label: Two-attack fire drake
briefs.why: A beast with a close claw strike and a long fire breath reads as two threats: close is fast, far is hot.
briefs.keep: two attack records (melee and ranged) with their own icon and strike count; one melee strip as a six-frame strike; per-creature death sound
briefs.change: a wingless crested quadruped with a glowing spine instead of wings; breath is a cone of ember sparks, not a flame column; our own strike timing with hitstop

briefs.label: Odds card
briefs.why: A preview that shows the chance to win before the player engages makes a duel readable at 375 wide.
briefs.keep: exact per-round odds for small fights; sampled estimate for big ones; slowed state as its own branch
briefs.change: a three-stop bar instead of a text table; no sampling until the odds card is opened; we drop the slow plane and use a stamina state

briefs.label: Faction ramp
briefs.why: One ramp per faction recolours every unit without new art; the minimap marker keeps the team readable at a glance.
briefs.keep: four values per faction (average, highlight, shadow, minimap marker); palette swap on one base sprite
briefs.change: a gold seam instead of a flat team colour; add a fifth value for a glow rim; ramp chosen by faction not player slot

briefs.label: Striking frame strip
briefs.why: One line in the data describes a whole strike, so a clip can be tuned without new art.
briefs.keep: frame range with per-frame time; a single strip for the whole strike
briefs.change: a three-part curve (wind-up, hit, recover) with a hitstop on the hit frame; no per-frame ms, but a curve per attack
